title: Microsoft Windows 3.1
summary: 16-bit graphical operating environment running on top of MS-DOS, introducing TrueType fonts, Minesweeper, and Object Linking and Embedding (OLE).
facts: Released in April 1992, selling over 3 million copies in its first two months.
Introduced TrueType scalable fonts making Windows a viable desktop publishing system.
Included Solitaire and Minesweeper to teach users drag-and-drop mouse skills.

title: Microsoft Windows 95
summary: Landmark 32-bit operating system featuring the Start Menu, Taskbar, Windows Explorer, Plug and Play architecture, and long filename support.
facts: Launched on August 24, 1995 with a $300M marketing campaign using the Rolling Stones song 'Start Me Up'.
Brian Eno composed the iconic 3.25-second Windows 95 startup sound.
Unified MS-DOS and Windows into a integrated GUI environment.

title: Microsoft Windows 98
summary: Consumer operating system featuring native USB support, FAT32 file system, Internet Explorer 4 integration, and DirectX 5 graphics acceleration.
facts: Featured the famous Blue Screen of Death (BSOD) demonstration glitch by Bill Gates at Comdex 1998.
Included Windows Driver Model (WDM) and system maintenance utilities like Disk Defragmenter.
Second Edition (SE) released in 1999 added Internet Connection Sharing (ICS).

title: Microsoft Windows NT 4.0
summary: 32-bit preemptive multitasking business and server operating system combining NT security kernel with the user interface of Windows 95.
facts: Released for Workstation and Server editions on x86, Alpha, MIPS, and PowerPC platforms.
Offered robust memory protection and NTFS file system security.
Core foundation for future consumer NT releases like Windows 2000 and XP.

title: Microsoft Internet Explorer 3.0 & 4.0
summary: Microsoft's web browsers that sparked the 'Browser Wars' against Netscape, featuring Active Desktop, CSS support, and tight OS bundling.
facts: IE 3.0 was released in August 1996 and introduced support for CSS and ActiveX controls.
IE 4.0 (1997) introduced Active Desktop and deep integration with Windows Explorer.
Triggered United States v. Microsoft Corp. antitrust litigation.
